# Induced abortion

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Obstetrics/gynecology > Pregnancy and prenatal care > Induced abortion*

[Original Article Link](/library/jG0__h)

---

## Summary

Induced abortion is the use of interventions to end a <u>pregnancy</u> and remove <u>products of conception</u> from the <u>uterus</u>. Common indications include patient choice, anticipated harm to the pregnant individual, and fetal genetic or anatomical abnormalities. A preabortion evaluation involves <u>confirmation of pregnancy</u> and determination of <u>gestational age</u>, with additional studies as indicated based on <u>patient history</u> and preferences. Uterine evacuation for induced abortion is achieved using the same medications and/or procedures that are used to manage <u>pregnancy loss</u>. A combined regimen of <u>mifepristone</u> and <u>misoprostol</u> is recommended for <u>medication abortion</u> in the first and <u>second trimester</u> of <u>pregnancy</u>. Recommended <u>procedural abortion</u> techniques are <u>uterine aspiration</u> in the <u>first trimester</u> and <u>dilation and evacuation</u> in the <u>second trimester</u>. Postabortion care involves monitoring for <u>complications of induced abortion</u> and providing additional care related to <u>family planning</u> and psychosocial support as indicated.

---

## Preabortion evaluation

* Confirm the <u>diagnosis of pregnancy</u>.

* Perform a <u>gestational age assessment</u>.

* Consider indications for induced abortion:

* Patient's choice to end the <u>pregnancy</u>

* Anticipated harm to the pregnant individual

* Genetic or anatomical abnormalities in the fetus  [[11]](/library/JXcs_a0)

* Perform additional studies, if indicated.

* <u>Ultrasound</u>: if <u>risk factors for ectopic pregnancy</u> or uncertain <u>gestational age</u>

* <u>Hemoglobin</u> and/or <u>hematocrit</u>: if concern for <u>anemia</u>

* <u>Screening for RhD alloimmunization in pregnancy</u>: if Rh status is unknown  [[6]](/library/e41xRS0)[[12]](/library/tOdX8J0)[[13]](/library/4nd3tq0)

* <u>STI testing</u>: in patients with symptoms or if requested

* Use <u>shared decision-making</u> to select a method for induced abortion.

* Offer <u>analgesia</u> and/or sedation based on the planned method.

* Discuss <u>family planning</u> and <u>contraception after spontaneous or induced abortion</u>.  [[14]](/library/GLdB_q0)

| <br><u>First trimester</u>  [[4]](/library/9P1NSS0)[[6]](/library/e41xRS0)[[17]](/library/eodxaI0)<br> | <br><br>* Preferred  [[4]](/library/9P1NSS0)[[6]](/library/e41xRS0)<br><br>* <u>Mifepristone</u> (<u>progesterone antagonist</u>) DOSAGE once<br><br>* PLUS <u>misoprostol</u> (<u>prostaglandin</u> analog) DOSAGE 24–48 hours later; additional doses as indicated  [[4]](/library/9P1NSS0)[[6]](/library/e41xRS0)<br><br>* Alternative: monotherapy with <u>misoprostol</u> (<u>off-label</u>) DOSAGE [[6]](/library/e41xRS0)[[16]](/library/VodGaI0)<br><br><br> | <br>* <u>Uterine aspiration</u> is preferred over other forms of <u>dilation and curettage</u>   [[2]](/library/8MdOqq0)[[6]](/library/e41xRS0)[[17]](/library/eodxaI0)<br><br> |
| <br><u>Second trimester</u> [[11]](/library/JXcs_a0)<br> | <br><br>* Preferred: <u>mifepristone</u> DOSAGE followed 24–48 hours later by a <u>prostaglandin</u> analog (e.g., <u>misoprostol</u>DOSAGE) [[6]](/library/e41xRS0)[[18]](/library/ILdY_q0)<br><br>* Alternatives<br><br>* <u>Misoprostol</u> monotherapy DOSAGE [[6]](/library/e41xRS0)[[18]](/library/ILdY_q0)<br><br>* <u>Oxytocin</u>: may be considered when <u>misoprostol</u> is unavailable<br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Dilation and evacuation</u><br><br>* Cervical preparation (e.g., osmotic dilators, <u>misoprostol</u>) is recommended.<br><br><br> |





> [!TIP]
> Prophylactic <u>antibiotics</u> should be provided for all procedural abortions, but are not indicated for <u>medication abortion</u>. [[11]](/library/JXcs_a0)




> [!TIP]
> A limited number of facilities in the US provide second-trimester abortions and these are almost always procedural. [[9]](/library/Tod6YI0)

## Complications

Complications are rare, including after self-managed <u>medication abortion</u> in the first-trimester. Risk of complications increases with later abortions and unsafe abortions. [[7]](/library/uMdpqq0)[[22]](/library/RodlbI0)[[23]](/library/bKdHUI0)




* <u>Retained products of conception</u>

* Hemorrhage

* Infection

* <u>Disseminated intravascular coagulation</u>

* <u>Pulmonary embolism</u>, <u>amniotic fluid embolism</u> [[24]](/library/c41aRS0)

* Additional complications of <u>procedural abortion</u> include:

* Cervical <u>laceration</u>

* Uterine perforation

* <u>Pelvic</u> organ damage





> [!TIP]
> Induced abortion does not increase the risk of mental health disorders, <u>infertility</u>, or <u>breast cancer</u>. [[22]](/library/RodlbI0)




We list the most important complications. The selection is not exhaustive.
